..
Issued at 330 AM CDT Wed Jul 15 2026

Weak 1020 mb surface high pressure ridge over Iowa and ridging
over central IL has brought clear skies and calm winds to CWA.
With temps cooling to near dewpoints in the upper 60s to around
70F, we are seeing patchy shallow ground fog developing past few
hours over the area. Latest model guidance like the HRRR, RAP13
and GFSLamp show patchy fog continuing to develop over central
IL through sunrise and could get locally dense in spots
especially south of I-74 to along I-72. The patchy fog should
lift quickly by mid morning similar to past few mornings. May
see patchy fog redevelop overnight into early Thu morning,
though latest CAMs show less visibilities restrictions over CWA
overnight than what they are showing early this morning. 

A Rex Block pattern continued over the central and eastern US
with a strong upper level ridge over the upper Midwest into the
Ohio river valley, and a weak upper level low/trof over the
Southern States. This has brought dry and very warm weather to 
central/se IL during the past few days along with a heat wave at
mid week. The strong 500 mb high to remain just north/ne of CWA
with our 500 mb heights of 594-597 decameters today (highest ne
of I-74). This should continued dry and hot weather today with 
mostly sunny skies as few to scattered cumulus clouds (3-5k ft 
bases) appear later morning/afternoon. Isolated convection 
should stay south of CWA over southern IL this afternoon/early 
evening mainly south of I-64. Highs in the lower 90s today with 
dewpoints in the low to mid 70s, giving afternoon heat indices 
peaking from 97-103F, highest from I-74 north. This will fall a 
few degrees shy of heat advisory criteria of 105F though heat 
advisories this afternoon are not too far away in central and 
northern Indiana along with air quality alerts (air quality 
alerts go into northeast IL too today and evening). Muggy lows 
overnight in the lower 70s. 

A weak disturbance moving into the mid MS river valley Thu to
gradually bring deeper tropical moisture northward into
central/se IL later tonight and Thu as PWATs increase to 1.75-2.2
inches Thu afternoon with weak SSW flow. Models continue to show
isolated to scattered showers/thunderstorms developing over 
central/southern IL Thu afternoon. We have 20-40% chance of
convection over CWA Thu afternoon, highest over southern/sw CWA
with the higher pops over southern/sw IL where WPC Day2 has
marginal risk of excessive rainfall. Canadian wildfires near the
MN border is sending smoke southward across WI/MI today and into
northeast parts of IL/IN tonight into Thu as backdoor cold front
moves into northeast IL tonight. We could see some smoke aloft
moving over central IL into Thu which will increase our cloud
cover some but the surface smoke and air quality issues should
mostly stay ne of CWA through Thu. Highs Thu in the lower 90s
with afternoon heat indices in the upper 90s/lower 100s again. 

The weak upper level trof/disturbances moves over IL on Friday
and brings our best chances of convection (60-80%) especially 
Fri afternoon. WPC Day3 ERO has marginal risk of excessive
rainfall over CWA on Friday especially afternoon hours. PWATs
are very high on Friday, from 2-2.4 inches. We have quarter to
half inch of qpf on Friday from IL river east and tenth to
quarter inch west of the IL river. Though some spots may see 
1-2 inches or more in a short time with slow moving cells. We 
have moderately strong instability but weak wind shear Fri, so a
few storms could produce gusty winds/wet microbursts. May also 
see strong cells Thu afternoon though best chance would be sw 
IL. Highs Friday in the upper 80s to near 90F and afternoon heat
indices in the upper 90s to around 100.  

Models are trending slower with existing this weak disturbance
on Saturday so we will likely continue chances of convection
especially eastern IL Sat afternoon. Another hot and humid day
Sat with highs in the lower 90s and afternoon heat index
readings peaking around or just above 100 degrees. A weakening
cold front dropping down through northern/ne IL toward 
central IL Sunday but still very warm and humid with highs in
the upper 80s to around 90F. SW flow on Monday returning the 
hot /humid air mass over central/se IL before a stronger cold 
front moves through Mon night into Tue bringing cooler and less 
humid air back into the region for middle of next week (next 
Tue-Thu). Also have 20-30% chance of convection Mon and Monday
night and may linger chances into Tuesday.

The Climate Prediction Center (CPC) 8-14 Day Outlook for July 
22-28 has a 33-40% chance of below normal temperatures over IL 
while precipitation during this week is trending near normal.
